title: Check if Array is Good
statement:
For a positive integer `n`, let `base[n]` be the array of length `n + 1` holding each of `1, 2, ..., n - 1` once and the value `n` twice; for instance `base[1] = [1, 1]` and `base[3] = [1, 2, 3, 3]`.

Given an integer array `nums`, return `true` if some `base[n]` can be reordered to give exactly `nums` (the same values with the same multiplicities), and `false` otherwise.
notes:
## Intuition

The length of `nums` fixes the only possible `n`: `base[n]` has `n + 1` elements, so `n = nums.length - 1`. After that it is pure counting: every value from 1 to `n - 1` must appear exactly once, `n` must appear exactly twice, and nothing larger than `n` may appear. Sorting `nums` and comparing it with `[1, 2, ..., n, n]` also works, but counting avoids the sort.

## Approach

1. Set `n = nums.length - 1` and make a zeroed `count` array for the values 0 to `n`.
2. Walk `nums`. Any `num > n` cannot belong to `base[n]`, so return `false`; otherwise add one to `count[num]`.
3. Check that each `value` from 1 to `n - 1` was seen exactly once.
4. Return whether `n` was seen exactly twice.

Because the counts add up to `n + 1`, steps 3 and 4 together leave no room for an extra or missing value.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [2, 1, 3]`, so `n = 2` and `count` covers 0 to 2. The first two values are counted, then `num = 3` is larger than `n`, so the function returns `false` at once: a good array of length 3 can only be `[1, 2, 2]` in some order.

## Complexity

- Time: O(m), where `m = nums.length`: one pass to count and one pass to check.
- Space: O(m) for `count`.

## Pitfalls

- Take `n` from the length, not the maximum: `[2, 1, 3]` has maximum 3 but only three elements, so it cannot be `base[3]`.
- A single element is never good, since the smallest base array, `[1, 1]`, already has two; here `n = 0` and every value is too big.
- Checking only which values occur (a set) is not enough: `[1, 1, 2]` contains 1 and 2, but 1 must appear once and 2 twice.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `n` | the only candidate, `nums.length - 1` |
| `count` | `count[v]` is how many times `v` appears in `nums` |
| `num` | the element being counted |
| `value` | each number from 1 to `n - 1` being checked |

narration.2: base[n] has n + 1 elements, so the length decides the only possible n.
narration.3: One counter for every value from 0 to n.
narration.5: A value above n can never appear in base[n].
narration.6: So the array cannot be good.
narration.8: Record one more occurrence of this value.
narration.10: Every value below n must be present...
narration.12: A missing or repeated small value breaks the pattern.
narration.15: Finally, n itself must appear exactly twice.
